source.title: Understanding the Role of Adversarial Regularization in Supervised Learning

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extracting relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper empirically measures generalization error in supervised and adversarially regularized networks and evaluates a norm-based generalization measure. It does not test random-label memorization or the listed architecture, optimizer, batch-size, and dropout claims.
record.gate_note: The experiments report relative generalization error for supervised versus adversarial regularization and test whether a bound based on top-layer Frobenius norm and hidden-layer distance from initialization explains the adversarial generalization gap. Gradient and empirical-risk comparisons are not rows for the stated claim versions. Figures 6 and 7 provide the relevant generalization results, but their plotted values are not recoverable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates adversarial regularization and a norm-based generalization bound, rather than any specified version. Width-dependent generalization gaps do not establish V2's test-error trend beyond zero training error; norm-based bounds and topology perturbations do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. The appendix's random-label training MSE does not establish V1's paired training and held-out accuracy behavior.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's generalization paraphrase is accurate: adversarial regularization can improve relative generalization error with sufficient expressive capacity, while the tested norm-based bound does not fully explain adversarial generalization. The authors leave generalization-gap and sample-complexity explanations open. Their broader conclusion also concerns accelerated optimization and convergence under stated assumptions.
record.recipe_differences: Studies supervised learning with adversarial regularization versus sole supervision, not the claim's random-label and natural-label generalization setup or its listed interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset (MNIST versus CIFAR10) and training approach (sole supervision versus adversarial regularization); the reported relative-generalization improvement is stated for networks with sufficient expressive power.

fits_no_version.finding: The combined top-layer norm and hidden-layer distance-from-initialization measure explains supervised generalization gaps according to the authors, but does not fully explain the adversarial gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The explanatory adequacy of this norm-based generalization measure depends on whether training includes adversarial regularization.

fits_no_version.finding: Adversarial regularization can improve relative generalization error on MNIST and CIFAR10 when networks have sufficient expressive power.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial regularization can reduce the study's scaled training-test loss gap relative to sole supervision.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix B reports training MSE of 0.004 after 1000 epochs for an adversarially trained network with 8192 hidden units on randomly labeled MNIST. It reports topology rather than paired classification accuracies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An adversarially trained two-layer network can attain low training MSE on randomly labeled MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix B examines persistence of sparse topology under Gaussian weight perturbations, without measuring perturbation-induced training error or its relationship to generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse topology in the studied adversarially trained networks persists under low and moderate Gaussian weight perturbations.

record.problems: Relevant generalization values are presented only in figures and are not numerically described in the text. The study says its bound does not fully explain the adversarial generalization error and leaves the explanation open. No uncertainty estimates for these results are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant generalization rows omitted. Gradient, empirical-risk, and convergence results are outside the claim versions and were not extracted.

untested.parts: Paired random-label and natural-label classification accuracies under the same architecture and recipe, including near-perfect random-label training accuracy, chance random-label held-out accuracy, and above-chance natural-label held-out accuracy.
Held-out classification error as width increases beyond an established zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out error and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied figure text does not expose numerical generalization curves. Neither width sweeps, optimizer citations, nor the use of architectures with convolutional layers supplies the comparisons required by V2–V4.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Test error across widths beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
